title: WEKA-Based Decision-Tree Model for User Subscription Plan Prediction
authors: Guban, J. C. R.; Menderico, C. D. R.; Montalban, D. M. G.
venue: Technological University of the Philippines - Manila
tldr: Develops a J48 decision-tree model in WEKA to predict streaming subscription plans from 2,500 user records, achieving 72% accuracy with country, age, and device as top predictors.
problem_and_motivation: Understanding user preferences in subscription plan selection is vital for data-driven strategies. Predictive models can inform plan design and targeted marketing but require interpretable outputs.
approach: Used dataset of 2,500 anonymized user records from a major streaming platform.
Features included age, gender, country, device type, and subscription start month.
Applied J48 decision-tree algorithm in WEKA for supervised classification.
Evaluated using accuracy, Kappa statistic, precision, recall, F-measure, and ROC area.
findings: num: Model achieved 72% overall accuracy in predicting Basic, Standard, or Premium plans.
Country was the most influential predictor, followed by age and device type.
Interpretable decision rules highlight complex attribute combinations.
Younger smartphone users subscribing later in year often chose Premium.
Older users on Smart TVs tended toward Standard or Basic tiers.

definitions.definition: WEKA implementation of C4.5 decision tree algorithm.
Measure of agreement between predicted and actual classifications.

topics.name: Classification Approaches for Financial Behavioral Profiles
topics.justification: Decision-tree classification of user preferences by demographic/behavioral attributes.

topics.name: Predictive Modeling in Personal Finance Systems
topics.justification: Predictive modeling approach transferable to finance subscription prediction.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Demonstrates interpretable decision-tree classification for user subscription prediction. Shows country, age, and device type as key determinants of plan choice. Provides example of transforming user data into actionable business insights.
directly_justifies: Decision trees provide interpretable subscription plan prediction rules.
Country, age, and device type are top predictors of plan choice.
limits: Limited to streaming data; not directly personal finance.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematically scanned all domains. Assigned 5.C high for classification. Assigned 6.A medium for predictive modeling. Rejected personal finance-specific topics as paper addresses streaming subscription prediction.

limitations: Only 72% accuracy leaves room for improvement.
No comparison with other algorithm types beyond J48.
remember_this: J48 decision tree achieves 72% accuracy for subscription prediction.
Country is the strongest predictor, followed by age and device.
Interpretable rules reveal complex user attribute combinations.
Younger smartphone users tend toward Premium subscriptions.
